articleTitle: Prediction of Events Means of Data Parallelism
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Mathematics and Computers in Science and Engineering (MACISE)
abstract: A new approach to the events, which are difficult to predict is considered in the article. For this so-called parallel data is used - data of various precursors, by means of which the certain event is predicted with some low probability. A "live" functioning of prediction process is also reviewed. Using of parallel data allows to use supercomputers not only for their initial purpose - performing many computations of high volume, but also for "live" processing of parallel data and as a main instrument fundamental style of parallel data.

Author Keywords: supercomputers, prediction, parallel data, expandable matrices

articleTitle: Study of the Motion Dynamics of Camera Fastening Platform for the Object of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Mathematics and Computers in Science and Engineering (MACISE)
abstract: The subject and at the same time the main purpose of this article is to create a mathematical model describing the phenomenon of dynamic movement of the holder (the subject), used to support the visual unit (camera) fitted to the UAV platform. In addition, the Kalman filter used in the considerations improved the waveforms of control signals and reduced the influence of undesired signals on the control processes of other systems that are equipped with unmanned aircraft. Based on the analysis of the UAV object, the mathematical model created and selected simulation tests, the final part of the paper summarizes and formulates practical conclusions reflecting the actual work of the UAV object.

Author Keywords: study, dynamic phenomena, gyro platform motion, unmanned aerial vehicle

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Heart Electrical Instabilities by Using Topology, Convex Analysis, Conceptual Spaces, Graph Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Mathematics and Computers in Science and Engineering (MACISE)
abstract: The graph theory, topology, convex analysis have been studied and applied to medicine, cardiology. Heart electrical instability has various causes. The di?erential diagnosis of it is based on qualitative and quantitative electrocardiogram (ECG) assessment. The purpose of this study was to formulate model, an algorithm for making diagnosis of heart electrical instability as oxymoron, fractal and anti-fractal, Moebius strip like processes by using discrete mathematics, graph theory, topology, convex analysis, multiple testing. We used algorithm for diagnosing heart electrical instability, which reduces to qualitative and quantitative analysis of ECG in standard, inverted, 3D (as rotation bodies of ECG's elements) forms; constructing graphs, including "Gift wrapping" algorithm; calculation distances between points, angles between graphs, and others; comparison of qualitative and quantitative characteristics of these graphs by selective multiple testing; formulation of the diagnostic conclusion. Characteristics of ECG by distance between points, perimeters, and angles of polygons of complexes allowed to determine peculiarities of electromagnetic picture, triggers and resonators of heart electrical instabilities. Thus, complex using of discrete mathematics, graph theory, topology, convex analysis, multiple testing allowed us to formulate an algorithm for making diagnosis of heart electrical instability as oxymoron, fractal and anti-fractal, Moebius strip like processes. Analysis of graphs as networks of node-waves with their ribs can be the basis for improving the quality of diagnosis and treatment the patients with heart rhythm and conduction disorders.

Author Keywords: mathematical modeling, heart electrical instability, diagnosis

articleTitle: Study of the Resistance of GNSS Satellite Navigation Receiver to the Operation of a Narrowband Interfering Signal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Mathematics and Computers in Science and Engineering (MACISE)
abstract: The article presents mathematical foundations and a description of the algorithm assessing the performance of GPS receivers in the circumstances of simultaneous reception of interfering signals. The main focus was on the analysis of the variant in which the interfering signal is a narrowband signal. Simulation tests were carried out using the Matlab simulation and GlabGNSS simulation package for different values of the bandwidth of the interfering signal indicated in the paper, as WB (5 Hz) and NB (2 Hz). The discussed method ensures effective implementation of disturbance processes both in the exact position accuracy determined by the disturbed receiver, as well as disrupts the processes of tracking and searching for SIS signals by the GPS satellite receiver. Based on the analysis, created mathematical models and conducted simulation research in the field of the subject of the study, the final part of the article presents practical conclusions resulting from the proposed solution.

Author Keywords: study, satellite navigation receiver, narrowband signal, interference

publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Mathematics and Computers in Science and Engineering (MACISE)
abstract: Let G be a group with identity e, R a commutative G-graded ring with unity 1 and M a G-graded R-module. In this article, graded gw-prime submodules of M are defined. This class of graded submodules is a generalization of graded weakly prime submodules. A graded R-module M is said to be graded gw-prime if whenever L is a graded R-submodule of M and x; y ϵ h(R) such that xyL = {0}, then either x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>L = {0} or y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>L = {0}. A graded R-submodule N of M is said to be graded gw-prime if M/N is a graded gw-prime R-module, i.e., if whenever L is a graded R-submodule of M and x; y ϵ h(R) such that xyL ⊆ N, then either x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>L ⊆ N or y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>L ⊆ N. Also, we introduce the concept of graded valuation modules; let R be a G-graded domain with quotient field F and M a G-graded torsion free R-module. For b = x/y ϵ F where x; y ϵ h(R) and for s ϵ h(M), we write bs ϵ M if there exists t ϵ h(M) such that xs = yt. Then M is said to be a graded valuation R-module if for each b = x/y ϵ K (x; y ϵ h(R)), we have either bM ⊆ M or b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> M ⊆ M. After studying general properties of graded gw-prime submodules, their relation with graded valuation modules are examined.

articleTitle: Patterns in DBMS from Modeling to the Language Support
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Mathematics and Computers in Science and Engineering (MACISE)
abstract: The aim of the article is continuing the work of authors with patterns in DBMS (Database Management System) from the modeling to the language support, which means is focused on representation of the patterns, manipulation with patterns and query patterns. The idea of how to store, manipulate and query patterns is not very new but still important, and many tasks are necessary to solve. Analog to the storing, manipulating and querying relations or object classes is obvious, but the way is not equal. Patterns have specific properties and characteristics that are necessary to consider. The main attention of the article is devoted to time series patterns and time series.

Author Keywords: DBMS, pattern, modeling, database, Times Series, Cluster

articleTitle: Understanding Gender Commuting Gap Using Geographic Visualization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Mathematics and Computers in Science and Engineering (MACISE)
abstract: This paper discusses the spatial patterns of gender commuting to work gap using geographic visualization. Geographic visualization is a tool to understand and communicate spatial patterns. Geographic visualization integrates many disciplines - cartography, image analysis, visualization in scientific computing, information visualization, exploratory data analysis and geographic information system. Commuting to work is a global phenomenon. It involves number of vehicles on the roads and the consequences of this transportation event have impacts on the population, environment and the economy. Commuting to work is associated with daily travel, long distance journey and more time on the road. GIS is a system capable of geographic visualizing, analyzing and modelling spatially referenced real world data. It provides a framework that models the interactions of real world objects in space and time to find existing patterns and predicts what will happen. All transportation related events and attributes have space and time coordinates attached to them. This paper reviews the application of GIS in geographic visualizing and analyzing spatial patterns of commuting to work using different modes of transport and gender. Data on commuting to work by motorized vehicles such as cars, buses, rail and underground trains in the United Kingdom by regions is used in this study. The sample includes all individuals in employment in the age group 16 to 64, with valid geographical coordinates of residence and work place in 2011. The discussion is focus on the commuting gap between male and female commuters by regions.

Author Keywords: geographic visualization, commuting to work, gender, spatial patterns, United Kingdom
